name: MindVote
description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used as scalable tools for pilot testing, predicting public opinion distributions before deploying costly surveys. To serve as effective pilot testing tools, the performance of these LLMs is typically benchmarked against their ability to reproduce the outcomes of past structured surveys. This evaluation paradigm, however, is misaligned with the dynamic, context-rich social media environments where public opinion is increasingly formed and expressed. By design, surveys strip away the social, cultural, and temporal context that shapes public opinion, and LLM benchmarks built on this paradigm inherit these critical limitations. To bridge this gap, we introduce MindVote, the first benchmark for public opinion distribution prediction grounded in authentic social media discourse. reputation: A new benchmark with emerging interest for evaluating LLMs on public-opinion forecasting from social media, but not yet broadly adopted.
notes: Text benchmark with probabilistic distribution targets rather than single-label answers; likely sensitive to temporal drift and platform/topic bias, and not a standard accuracy-style task.
